study_identification_part.si_4_title: Predicting Mental and Neurological Illnesses Based on Cerebellar Normative Features

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used five clinical datasets obtained from ABIDE I and II (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I and II), ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative), AIBL (The Australian Imaging, Biomarkers and Lifestyle Flagship Study), DEMGEN (Norwegian Dementia Genetics Network), and TOP (Thematically Organized Psychosis). The normative model was pre-trained using a publicly available cerebellar normative model based on >27,000 individuals without diagnoses from Kim et al. 2024 (reference 15). The training set consisted of 27,117 participants from 132 scanning sites.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "The clinical datasets were obtained from the ABIDE I and II (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I and II), ADNI (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative), AIBL (The Australian Imaging, Biomarkers and Lifestyle Flagship Study), DEMGEN (Norwegian Dementia Genetics Network), and TOP (Thematically Organized Psychosis) cohorts."; "We used a publicly available cerebellar normative model based on >27,000 individuals without diagnoses (15)."

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: This study used a pre-trained cerebellar normative model from Kim et al. 2024. The normative model was trained on 27,117 healthy individuals and tested on 26,985 healthy individuals. Clinical datasets (ABIDE I/II for ASD, ADNI/AIBL/DEMGEN for AD and MCI, TOP for BD and SZ) were used as transfer sets for clinical classification research. Matched healthy controls were selected from the test set using nearest-neighbor matching based on sex, scanning site, and age.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "The study sample consisted of individuals from the cerebellar lifespan normative model (15), where individuals without a diagnosis were split into a training set (n = 27,117; 54% female), a test set (n = 26,985; 53% females), and a clinical set (n = 1757; 30% females) ... Individuals without diagnoses were matched to the clinical datasets of patients with AD, ASD, BD, MCI, and SZ"

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: This study used a pre-trained cerebellar normative model from Kim et al. 2024 (reference 15). The overall healthy control sample was 54,102 participants (training set: 27,117, testing set: 26,985) from 132 scanning sites. The clinical set (n=1,757) was not used in normative model construction but for subsequent classification tasks.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Training set: mean 54.36, SD 20.31. Testing set: mean 54.52, SD 20.19. The overall weighted mean was calculated as (27117*54.36 + 26985*54.52)/(27117+26985) = 54.44. The pooled SD was calculated as sqrt(((27117-1)*20.31^2 + (26985-1)*20.19^2)/(27117+26985-2)) = 20.25. The normative model spans ages 3 to 85 years as stated in the main text.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Training set: 53%F:47%M (n=27,117), calculated as female_n = 27117*0.53 = 14,372 (inferred), male_n = 27117*0.47 = 12,745 (inferred). Testing set: 53%F:47%M (n=26,985), calculated as female_n = 26985*0.53 = 14,302 (inferred), male_n = 26985*0.47 = 12,683 (inferred). Overall: female_n = 14372+14302 = 28,674, male_n = 12745+12683 = 25,428. The main text states the training set was 54% female, while Supplementary Table 2 states 53:47. We use the supplementary table values as they are more detailed.
